<h3 id="create-an-international-payment-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-idempotency-key|header|string|true|Every request will be processed only once per x-idempotency-key.  The<br>Idempotency Key will be valid for 24 hours.<br>|
|x-jws-signature|header|string|true|A detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|
|body|body|[OBWriteInternationalConsent5](#schemaobwriteinternationalconsent5)|true|Default|
|» Data|body|object|true|none|
|» » ReadRefundAccount|body|string|false|Specifies to share the refund account details with PISP|
|» » Initiation|body|object|true|The Initiation payload is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP. It is used to request movement of funds from the debtor account to a creditor for a single international payment.|
|» » » InstructionIdentification|body|string|true|Unique identification as assigned by an instructing party for an instructed party to unambiguously identify the instruction.<br>Usage: the  instruction identification is a point to point reference that can be used between the instructing party and the instructed party to refer to the individual instruction. It can be included in several messages related to the instruction.|
|» » » EndToEndIdentification|body|string|true|Unique identification assigned by the initiating party to unambiguously identify the transaction. This identification is passed on, unchanged, throughout the entire end-to-end chain.<br>Usage: The end-to-end identification can be used for reconciliation or to link tasks relating to the transaction. It can be included in several messages related to the transaction.<br>OB: The Faster Payments Scheme can only access 31 characters for the EndToEndIdentification field.|
|» » » LocalInstrument|body|[OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code](#schemaobinternallocalinstrument1code)|false|User community specific instrument.<br>Usage: This element is used to specify a local instrument, local clearing option and/or further qualify the service or service level. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » InstructionPriority|body|string|false|Indicator of the urgency or order of importance that the instructing party would like the instructed party to apply to the processing of the instruction.|
|» » » ExtendedPurpose|body|string|false|Specifies the purpose of an international payment, when there is no corresponding 4 character code available in the ISO20022 list of Purpose Codes.|
|» » » ChargeBearer|body|[OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code](#schemaobinternalchargebearertype1code)|false|Specifies which party/parties will bear the charges associated with the processing of the payment transaction. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » CurrencyOfTransfer|body|string|true|Specifies the currency of the to be transferred amount, which is different from the currency of the debtor's account.|
|» » » DestinationCountryCode|body|string|false|Country in which Credit Account is domiciled. Code to identify a country, a dependency, or another area of particular geopolitical interest, on the basis of country names obtained from the United Nations (ISO 3166, Alpha-2 code).|
|» » » InstructedAmount|body|object|true|Amount of money to be moved between the debtor and creditor, before deduction of charges, expressed in the currency as ordered by the initiating party.<br>Usage: This amount has to be transported unchanged through the transaction chain.|
|» » » » Amount|body|[OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType](#schemaobactivecurrencyandamount_simpletype)|true|A number of monetary units specified in an active currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.|
|» » » » Currency|body|[ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode](#schemaactiveorhistoriccurrencycode)|true|A code allocated to a currency by a Maintenance Agency under an international identification scheme, as described in the latest edition of the international standard ISO 4217 "Codes for the representation of currencies and funds".|
|» » » ExchangeRateInformation|body|object|false|Provides details on the currency exchange rate and contract.|
|» » » » UnitCurrency|body|string|true|Currency in which the rate of exchange is expressed in a currency exchange. In the example 1GBP = xxxCUR, the unit currency is GBP.|
|» » » » ExchangeRate|body|number|false|The factor used for conversion of an amount from one currency to another. This reflects the price at which one currency was bought with another currency.|
|» » » » RateType|body|string|true|Specifies the type used to complete the currency exchange.|
|» » » » ContractIdentification|body|string|false|Unique and unambiguous reference to the foreign exchange contract agreed between the initiating party/creditor and the debtor agent.|
|» » » DebtorAccount|body|object|false|Unambiguous identification of the account of the debtor to which a debit entry will be made as a result of the transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level, as displayed by the ASPSP's online channels.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » Creditor|body|object|false|Party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|Name by which a party is known and which is usually used to identify that party.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAgent|body|object|false|Financial institution servicing an account for the creditor.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalFinancialInstitutionIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalfinancialinstitutionidentification4code)|false|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list.|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_1](#schemaidentification_1)|false|Unique identification, as assigned by the creditor, to unambiguously identify the mandate.|
|» » » » Name|body|[Name](#schemaname)|false|Name by which an agent is known and which is usually used to identify that agent.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAccount|body|object|true|Unambiguous identification of the account of the creditor to which a credit entry will be posted as a result of the payment transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|true|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.<br>OB: ASPSPs may carry out name validation for Confirmation of Payee, but it is not mandatory.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » UltimateCreditor|body|[OBUltimateCreditor1](#schemaobultimatecreditor1)|false|Ultimate party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » UltimateDebtor|body|[OBUltimateDebtor1](#schemaobultimatedebtor1)|false|Ultimate party that owes an amount of money to the (ultimate) creditor.|
|» » » RegulatoryReporting|body|[[OBRegulatoryReporting1](#schemaobregulatoryreporting1)]|false|none|
|» » » RemittanceInformation|body|[OBRemittanceInformation2](#schemaobremittanceinformation2)|false|Information supplied to enable the matching of an entry with the items that the transfer is intended to settle, such as commercial invoices in an accounts' receivable system|
|» » » SupplementaryData|body|[OBSupplementaryData1](#schemaobsupplementarydata1)|false|Additional information that can not be captured in the structured fields and/or any other specific block.|
|» » Authorisation|body|object|false|The authorisation type request from the TPP.|
|» » » AuthorisationType|body|string|true|Type of authorisation flow requested.|
|» » » CompletionDateTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Date and time at which the requested authorisation flow must be completed. All dates in the JSON payloads are represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. <br>All date-time fields in responses must include the timezone. An example is below:<br>2017-04-05T10:43:07+00:00|
|» » SCASupportData|body|[OBSCASupportData1](#schemaobscasupportdata1)|false|Supporting Data provided by TPP, when requesting SCA Exemption.|
|» Risk|body|[OBRisk1](#schemaobrisk1)|true|The Risk section is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP.<br>It is used to specify additional details for risk scoring for Payments.|

## Get an International Payment Consent

<a id="opIdGetInternationalPaymentConsentsConsentId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-payment-consents/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-payment-consents/{ConsentId}`

Enables a PISP to retrieve the status of an intent to initiate an International Payment.

<h3 id="get-an-international-payment-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

## Confirm Funds Availability for an International Payment

<a id="opIdGetInternationalPaymentConsentsConsentIdFundsConfirmation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-payment-consents/string/funds-confirmation \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-payment-consents/{ConsentId}/funds-confirmation`

Enables a PISP to check whether a PSU has sufficient available funds for an International Payment.

<h3 id="confirm-funds-availability-for-an-international-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|

|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

|200|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|
|200|RateLimit-Policy|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A non-empty list of Quota Policy Items. The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|200|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|
|400|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|400|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|
|401|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|403|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|403|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|
|404|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|405|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|406|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|429|Retry-After|integer||Number in seconds to wait|
|429|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|500|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|500|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
PSUOAuth2Security ( Scopes: payments )
</aside>

<h3 id="initiate-an-international-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-idempotency-key|header|string|true|Every request will be processed only once per x-idempotency-key.  The<br>Idempotency Key will be valid for 24 hours.<br>|
|x-jws-signature|header|string|true|A detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|
|body|body|[OBWriteInternational3](#schemaobwriteinternational3)|true|Default|
|» Data|body|object|true|none|
|» » ConsentId|body|string|true|OB: Unique identification as assigned by the ASPSP to uniquely identify the consent resource.|
|» » Initiation|body|object|true|The Initiation payload is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP. It is used to request movement of funds from the debtor account to a creditor for a single international payment.|
|» » » InstructionIdentification|body|string|true|Unique identification as assigned by an instructing party for an instructed party to unambiguously identify the instruction.<br>Usage: the  instruction identification is a point to point reference that can be used between the instructing party and the instructed party to refer to the individual instruction. It can be included in several messages related to the instruction.|
|» » » EndToEndIdentification|body|string|true|Unique identification assigned by the initiating party to unambiguously identify the transaction. This identification is passed on, unchanged, throughout the entire end-to-end chain.<br>Usage: The end-to-end identification can be used for reconciliation or to link tasks relating to the transaction. It can be included in several messages related to the transaction.<br>OB: The Faster Payments Scheme can only access 31 characters for the EndToEndIdentification field.|
|» » » LocalInstrument|body|[OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code](#schemaobinternallocalinstrument1code)|false|User community specific instrument.<br>Usage: This element is used to specify a local instrument, local clearing option and/or further qualify the service or service level. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » InstructionPriority|body|string|false|Indicator of the urgency or order of importance that the instructing party would like the instructed party to apply to the processing of the instruction.|
|» » » ExtendedPurpose|body|string|false|Specifies the purpose of an international payment, when there is no corresponding 4 character code available in the ISO20022 list of Purpose Codes.|
|» » » ChargeBearer|body|[OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code](#schemaobinternalchargebearertype1code)|false|Specifies which party/parties will bear the charges associated with the processing of the payment transaction. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » CurrencyOfTransfer|body|string|true|Specifies the currency of the to be transferred amount, which is different from the currency of the debtor's account.|
|» » » DestinationCountryCode|body|string|false|Country in which Credit Account is domiciled. Code to identify a country, a dependency, or another area of particular geopolitical interest, on the basis of country names obtained from the United Nations (ISO 3166, Alpha-2 code).|
|» » » InstructedAmount|body|object|true|Amount of money to be moved between the debtor and creditor, before deduction of charges, expressed in the currency as ordered by the initiating party.<br>Usage: This amount has to be transported unchanged through the transaction chain.|
|» » » » Amount|body|[OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType](#schemaobactivecurrencyandamount_simpletype)|true|A number of monetary units specified in an active currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.|
|» » » » Currency|body|[ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode](#schemaactiveorhistoriccurrencycode)|true|A code allocated to a currency by a Maintenance Agency under an international identification scheme, as described in the latest edition of the international standard ISO 4217 "Codes for the representation of currencies and funds".|
|» » » ExchangeRateInformation|body|object|false|Provides details on the currency exchange rate and contract.|
|» » » » UnitCurrency|body|string|true|Currency in which the rate of exchange is expressed in a currency exchange. In the example 1GBP = xxxCUR, the unit currency is GBP.|
|» » » » ExchangeRate|body|number|false|The factor used for conversion of an amount from one currency to another. This reflects the price at which one currency was bought with another currency.|
|» » » » RateType|body|string|true|Specifies the type used to complete the currency exchange.|
|» » » » ContractIdentification|body|string|false|Unique and unambiguous reference to the foreign exchange contract agreed between the initiating party/creditor and the debtor agent.|
|» » » DebtorAccount|body|object|false|Unambiguous identification of the account of the debtor to which a debit entry will be made as a result of the transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level, as displayed by the ASPSP's online channels.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » Creditor|body|object|false|Party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|Name by which a party is known and which is usually used to identify that party.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAgent|body|object|false|Financial institution servicing an account for the creditor.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalFinancialInstitutionIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalfinancialinstitutionidentification4code)|false|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list.|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_1](#schemaidentification_1)|false|Unique identification, as assigned by the creditor, to unambiguously identify the mandate.|
|» » » » Name|body|[Name](#schemaname)|false|Name by which an agent is known and which is usually used to identify that agent.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAccount|body|object|true|Unambiguous identification of the account of the creditor to which a credit entry will be posted as a result of the payment transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|true|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.<br>OB: ASPSPs may carry out name validation for Confirmation of Payee, but it is not mandatory.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » UltimateCreditor|body|[OBUltimateCreditor1](#schemaobultimatecreditor1)|false|Ultimate party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » UltimateDebtor|body|[OBUltimateDebtor1](#schemaobultimatedebtor1)|false|Ultimate party that owes an amount of money to the (ultimate) creditor.|
|» » » RegulatoryReporting|body|[[OBRegulatoryReporting1](#schemaobregulatoryreporting1)]|false|none|
|» » » RemittanceInformation|body|[OBRemittanceInformation2](#schemaobremittanceinformation2)|false|Information supplied to enable the matching of an entry with the items that the transfer is intended to settle, such as commercial invoices in an accounts' receivable system|
|» » » SupplementaryData|body|[OBSupplementaryData1](#schemaobsupplementarydata1)|false|Additional information that can not be captured in the structured fields and/or any other specific block.|
|» Risk|body|[OBRisk1](#schemaobrisk1)|true|The Risk section is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP.<br>It is used to specify additional details for risk scoring for Payments.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » InstructionPriority|Normal|
|» » » InstructionPriority|Urgent|
|» » » ChargeBearer|BorneByCreditor|
|» » » ChargeBearer|BorneByDebtor|
|» » » ChargeBearer|FollowingServiceLevel|
|» » » ChargeBearer|Shared|
|» » » » RateType|Actual|
|» » » » RateType|Agreed|
|» » » » RateType|Indicative|

|201|RateLimit-Policy|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A non-empty list of Quota Policy Items. The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|201|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
PSUOAuth2Security ( Scopes: payments )
</aside>

## Get an International Payment

<a id="opIdGetInternationalPaymentsInternationalPaymentId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-payments/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-payments/{InternationalPaymentId}`

Enables a PISP to retrieve the status of an International Payment.

<h3 id="get-an-international-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|InternationalPaymentId|path|string|true|InternationalPaymentId|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

## Get details of an International Payment

<a id="opIdGetInternationalPaymentsInternationalPaymentIdPaymentDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-payments/string/payment-details \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-payments/{InternationalPaymentId}/payment-details`

Enables a PISP to retrieve detailed information on the status of an International Payment.

<h3 id="get-details-of-an-international-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|InternationalPaymentId|path|string|true|InternationalPaymentId|

|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|201|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|201|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|
|201|RateLimit-Policy|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A non-empty list of Quota Policy Items. The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|201|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|

## Get an International Scheduled Payment Consent

<a id="opIdGetInternationalScheduledPaymentConsentsConsentId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-scheduled-payment-consents/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-scheduled-payment-consents/{ConsentId}`

Enables a PISP to retrieve the status of an intent to initiate an International Scheduled Payment.

<h3 id="get-an-international-scheduled-payment-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ConsentId|path|string|true|ConsentId|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|

|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

## Confirm Funds Availability for an International Scheduled Payment

<a id="opIdGetInternationalScheduledPaymentConsentsConsentIdFundsConfirmation"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-scheduled-payment-consents/string/funds-confirmation \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-scheduled-payment-consents/{ConsentId}/funds-confirmation`

Enables a PISP to check whether a PSU has sufficient available funds for an International Scheduled Payment.

<h3 id="initiate-an-international-scheduled-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-idempotency-key|header|string|true|Every request will be processed only once per x-idempotency-key.  The<br>Idempotency Key will be valid for 24 hours.<br>|
|x-jws-signature|header|string|true|A detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|
|body|body|[OBWriteInternationalScheduled3](#schemaobwriteinternationalscheduled3)|true|Default|
|» Data|body|object|true|none|
|» » ConsentId|body|string|true|OB: Unique identification as assigned by the ASPSP to uniquely identify the consent resource.|
|» » Initiation|body|object|true|The Initiation payload is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP. It is used to request movement of funds from the debtor account to a creditor for a single scheduled international payment.|
|» » » InstructionIdentification|body|string|true|Unique identification as assigned by an instructing party for an instructed party to unambiguously identify the instruction.<br>Usage: the  instruction identification is a point to point reference that can be used between the instructing party and the instructed party to refer to the individual instruction. It can be included in several messages related to the instruction.|
|» » » EndToEndIdentification|body|string|false|Unique identification assigned by the initiating party to unambiguously identify the transaction. This identification is passed on, unchanged, throughout the entire end-to-end chain.<br>Usage: The end-to-end identification can be used for reconciliation or to link tasks relating to the transaction. It can be included in several messages related to the transaction.<br>OB: The Faster Payments Scheme can only access 31 characters for the EndToEndIdentification field.|
|» » » LocalInstrument|body|[OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code](#schemaobinternallocalinstrument1code)|false|User community specific instrument.<br>Usage: This element is used to specify a local instrument, local clearing option and/or further qualify the service or service level. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalLocalInstrument1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » InstructionPriority|body|string|false|Indicator of the urgency or order of importance that the instructing party would like the instructed party to apply to the processing of the instruction.|
|» » » ExtendedPurpose|body|string|false|Specifies the purpose of an international payment, when there is no corresponding 4 character code available in the ISO20022 list of Purpose Codes.|
|» » » ChargeBearer|body|[OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code](#schemaobinternalchargebearertype1code)|false|Specifies which party/parties will bear the charges associated with the processing of the payment transaction. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » RequestedExecutionDateTime|body|string(date-time)|true|Date at which the initiating party requests the clearing agent to process the payment. <br>Usage: This is the date on which the debtor's account is to be debited. All dates in the JSON payloads are represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. <br>All date-time fields in responses must include the timezone. An example is below:<br>2017-04-05T10:43:07+00:00|
|» » » CurrencyOfTransfer|body|string|true|Specifies the currency of the to be transferred amount, which is different from the currency of the debtor's account.|
|» » » DestinationCountryCode|body|string|false|Country in which Credit Account is domiciled. Code to identify a country, a dependency, or another area of particular geopolitical interest, on the basis of country names obtained from the United Nations (ISO 3166, Alpha-2 code).|
|» » » InstructedAmount|body|object|true|Amount of money to be moved between the debtor and creditor, before deduction of charges, expressed in the currency as ordered by the initiating party.<br>Usage: This amount has to be transported unchanged through the transaction chain.|
|» » » » Amount|body|[OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType](#schemaobactivecurrencyandamount_simpletype)|true|A number of monetary units specified in an active currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.|
|» » » » Currency|body|[ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode](#schemaactiveorhistoriccurrencycode)|true|A code allocated to a currency by a Maintenance Agency under an international identification scheme, as described in the latest edition of the international standard ISO 4217 "Codes for the representation of currencies and funds".|
|» » » ExchangeRateInformation|body|object|false|Provides details on the currency exchange rate and contract.|
|» » » » UnitCurrency|body|string|true|Currency in which the rate of exchange is expressed in a currency exchange. In the example 1GBP = xxxCUR, the unit currency is GBP.|
|» » » » ExchangeRate|body|number|false|The factor used for conversion of an amount from one currency to another. This reflects the price at which one currency was bought with another currency.|
|» » » » RateType|body|string|true|Specifies the type used to complete the currency exchange.|
|» » » » ContractIdentification|body|string|false|Unique and unambiguous reference to the foreign exchange contract agreed between the initiating party/creditor and the debtor agent.|
|» » » DebtorAccount|body|object|false|Unambiguous identification of the account of the debtor to which a debit entry will be made as a result of the transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level, as displayed by the ASPSP's online channels.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » Creditor|body|object|false|Party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|Name by which a party is known and which is usually used to identify that party.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAgent|body|object|false|Financial institution servicing an account for the creditor.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalFinancialInstitutionIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalfinancialinstitutionidentification4code)|false|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list.|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_1](#schemaidentification_1)|false|Unique identification, as assigned by the creditor, to unambiguously identify the mandate.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » Name|body|[Name](#schemaname)|false|Name by which an agent is known and which is usually used to identify that agent.|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAccount|body|object|true|Unambiguous identification of the account of the creditor to which a credit entry will be posted as a result of the payment transaction.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|true|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.<br>OB: ASPSPs may carry out name validation for Confirmation of Payee, but it is not mandatory.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » UltimateCreditor|body|[OBUltimateCreditor1](#schemaobultimatecreditor1)|false|Ultimate party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » UltimateDebtor|body|[OBUltimateDebtor1](#schemaobultimatedebtor1)|false|Ultimate party that owes an amount of money to the (ultimate) creditor.|
|» » » RegulatoryReporting|body|[[OBRegulatoryReporting1](#schemaobregulatoryreporting1)]|false|none|
|» » » RemittanceInformation|body|[OBRemittanceInformation2](#schemaobremittanceinformation2)|false|Information supplied to enable the matching of an entry with the items that the transfer is intended to settle, such as commercial invoices in an accounts' receivable system|
|» » » SupplementaryData|body|[OBSupplementaryData1](#schemaobsupplementarydata1)|false|Additional information that can not be captured in the structured fields and/or any other specific block.|
|» Risk|body|[OBRisk1](#schemaobrisk1)|true|The Risk section is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP.<br>It is used to specify additional details for risk scoring for Payments.|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|200|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|
|200|RateLimit-Policy|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A non-empty list of Quota Policy Items. The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|200|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|
|400|x-fapi-interaction-id|string||An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|400|x-jws-signature|string||Header containing a detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.<br>|

<h3 id="create-an-international-standing-order-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-idempotency-key|header|string|true|Every request will be processed only once per x-idempotency-key.  The<br>Idempotency Key will be valid for 24 hours.<br>|
|x-jws-signature|header|string|true|A detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|
|body|body|[OBWriteInternationalStandingOrderConsent6](#schemaobwriteinternationalstandingorderconsent6)|true|Default|
|» Data|body|object|true|none|
|» » Permission|body|string|true|Specifies the Open Banking service request types.|
|» » ReadRefundAccount|body|string|false|Specifies to share the refund account details with PISP|
|» » Initiation|body|object|true|The Initiation payload is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP. It is used to request movement of funds from the debtor account to a creditor for an international standing order.|
|» » » RemittanceInformation|body|[OBRemittanceInformation2](#schemaobremittanceinformation2)|false|Information supplied to enable the matching of an entry with the items that the transfer is intended to settle, such as commercial invoices in an accounts' receivable system|
|» » » NumberOfPayments|body|[NumberOfPayments](#schemanumberofpayments)|false|Number of the payments that will be made in completing this frequency sequence including any executed since the sequence start date.|
|» » » ExtendedPurpose|body|string|false|Specifies the purpose of an international payment, when there is no corresponding 4 character code available in the ISO20022 list of Purpose Codes.|
|» » » ChargeBearer|body|[OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code](#schemaobinternalchargebearertype1code)|false|Specifies which party/parties will bear the charges associated with the processing of the payment transaction. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » CurrencyOfTransfer|body|string|true|Specifies the currency of the to be transferred amount, which is different from the currency of the debtor's account.|
|» » » DestinationCountryCode|body|string|false|Country in which Credit Account is domiciled. Code to identify a country, a dependency, or another area of particular geopolitical interest, on the basis of country names obtained from the United Nations (ISO 3166, Alpha-2 code).|
|» » » InstructedAmount|body|object|true|Amount of money to be moved between the debtor and creditor, before deduction of charges, expressed in the currency as ordered by the initiating party.<br>Usage: This amount has to be transported unchanged through the transaction chain.|
|» » » » Amount|body|[OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType](#schemaobactivecurrencyandamount_simpletype)|true|A number of monetary units specified in an active currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.|
|» » » » Currency|body|[ActiveOrHistoricCurrencyCode](#schemaactiveorhistoriccurrencycode)|true|A code allocated to a currency by a Maintenance Agency under an international identification scheme, as described in the latest edition of the international standard ISO 4217 "Codes for the representation of currencies and funds".|
|» » » DebtorAccount|body|object|false|Provides the details to identify the debtor account.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level, as displayed by the ASPSP's online channels.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » Creditor|body|object|false|Party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|false|Name by which a party is known and which is usually used to identify that party.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAgent|body|object|false|Party that manages the account on behalf of the account owner, that is manages the registration and booking of entries on the account, calculates balances on the account and provides information about the account.<br>This is the servicer of the beneficiary account.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalFinancialInstitutionIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalfinancialinstitutionidentification4code)|false|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list.|
|» » » » Identification|body|string|false|Unique and unambiguous identification of the servicing institution.|
|» » » » Name|body|[Name](#schemaname)|false|Name by which an agent is known and which is usually used to identify that agent.|
|» » » » LEI|body|[LEI](#schemalei)|false|Legal entity identification as an alternate identification for a party. Legal Entity Identifier is a code allocated to a party as described in ISO 17442 "Financial Services - Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)".|
|» » » » PostalAddress|body|[OBPostalAddress7](#schemaobpostaladdress7)|false|Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.|
|» » » CreditorAccount|body|object|true|Provides the details to identify the beneficiary account.|
|» » » » SchemeName|body|[OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code](#schemaobinternalaccountidentification4code)|true|Name of the identification scheme, in a coded form as published in an external list. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAccountIdentification4Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » » Identification|body|[Identification_0](#schemaidentification_0)|true|Identification assigned by an institution to identify an account. This identification is known by the account owner.|
|» » » » Name|body|string|true|The account name is the name or names of the account owner(s) represented at an account level.<br>Note, the account name is not the product name or the nickname of the account.<br>OB: ASPSPs may carry out name validation for Confirmation of Payee, but it is not mandatory.|
|» » » » SecondaryIdentification|body|[SecondaryIdentification](#schemasecondaryidentification)|false|This is secondary identification of the account, as assigned by the account servicing institution. <br>This can be used by building societies to additionally identify accounts with a roll number (in addition to a sort code and account number combination).|
|» » » » Proxy|body|[OBProxy1](#schemaobproxy1)|false|Specifies an alternate assumed name for the identification of the account.|
|» » » UltimateCreditor|body|[OBUltimateCreditor1](#schemaobultimatecreditor1)|false|Ultimate party to which an amount of money is due.|
|» » » UltimateDebtor|body|[OBUltimateDebtor1](#schemaobultimatedebtor1)|false|Ultimate party that owes an amount of money to the (ultimate) creditor.|
|» » » RegulatoryReporting|body|[[OBRegulatoryReporting1](#schemaobregulatoryreporting1)]|false|none|
|» » » MandateRelatedInformation|body|[OBMandateRelatedInformation1](#schemaobmandaterelatedinformation1)|true|none|
|» » » SupplementaryData|body|[OBSupplementaryData1](#schemaobsupplementarydata1)|false|Additional information that can not be captured in the structured fields and/or any other specific block.|
|» » Authorisation|body|object|false|The authorisation type request from the TPP.|
|» » » AuthorisationType|body|string|true|Type of authorisation flow requested.|
|» » » CompletionDateTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Date and time at which the requested authorisation flow must be completed. All dates in the JSON payloads are represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. <br>All date-time fields in responses must include the timezone. An example is below:<br>2017-04-05T10:43:07+00:00|
|» » SCASupportData|body|[OBSCASupportData1](#schemaobscasupportdata1)|false|Supporting Data provided by TPP, when requesting SCA Exemption.|
|» Risk|body|[OBRisk1](#schemaobrisk1)|true|The Risk section is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP.<br>It is used to specify additional details for risk scoring for Payments.|

## Get an International Standing Order Consent

<a id="opIdGetInternationalStandingOrderConsentsConsentId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-standing-order-consents/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-standing-order-consents/{ConsentId}`

Enables a PISP to retrieve the status of an intent to initiate an International Standing Order arrangement.

<h3 id="get-an-international-standing-order-consent-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ConsentId|path|string|true|ConsentId|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|200|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|

<h3 id="submit-an-international-standing-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-idempotency-key|header|string|true|Every request will be processed only once per x-idempotency-key.  The<br>Idempotency Key will be valid for 24 hours.<br>|
|x-jws-signature|header|string|true|A detached JWS signature of the body of the payload.|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|
|body|body|[OBWriteInternationalStandingOrder4](#schemaobwriteinternationalstandingorder4)|true|Default|
|» Data|body|object|true|none|
|» » ConsentId|body|string|true|OB: Unique identification as assigned by the ASPSP to uniquely identify the consent resource.|
|» » Initiation|body|object|true|The Initiation payload is sent by the initiating party to the ASPSP. It is used to request movement of funds from the debtor account to a creditor for an international standing order.|
|» » » RemittanceInformation|body|[OBRemittanceInformation2](#schemaobremittanceinformation2)|false|Information supplied to enable the matching of an entry with the items that the transfer is intended to settle, such as commercial invoices in an accounts' receivable system|
|» » » NumberOfPayments|body|[NumberOfPayments](#schemanumberofpayments)|false|Number of the payments that will be made in completing this frequency sequence including any executed since the sequence start date.|
|» » » ExtendedPurpose|body|string|false|Specifies the purpose of an international payment, when there is no corresponding 4 character code available in the ISO20022 list of Purpose Codes.|
|» » » ChargeBearer|body|[OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code](#schemaobinternalchargebearertype1code)|false|Specifies which party/parties will bear the charges associated with the processing of the payment transaction. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalChargeBearerType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|» » » CurrencyOfTransfer|body|string|true|Specifies the currency of the to be transferred amount, which is different from the currency of the debtor's account.|
|» » » DestinationCountryCode|body|string|false|Country in which Credit Account is domiciled. Code to identify a country, a dependency, or another area of particular geopolitical interest, on the basis of country names obtained from the United Nations (ISO 3166, Alpha-2 code).|
|» » » InstructedAmount|body|object|true|Amount of money to be moved between the debtor and creditor, before deduction of charges, expressed in the currency as ordered by the initiating party.<br>Usage: This amount has to be transported unchanged through the transaction chain.|
|» » » » Amount|body|[OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType](#schemaobactivecurrencyandamount_simpletype)|true|A number of monetary units specified in an active currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.|

|201|RateLimit-Policy|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A non-empty list of Quota Policy Items. The Item value __MUST__ be a String.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=100;w=10`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "q" parameter indicates the quota allocated by this policy measured in quota units.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "w" parameter value conveys a time window.<br>|
|201|RateLimit|string||TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>A server uses the "RateLimit" response header field to communicate the current service limit for a quota policy for a particular partition key.<br><br>Example:<br>`RateLimit: "default";r=50;t=30`<br><br>The **REQUIRED** "r" parameter value conveys the remaining quota units for the identified policy.<br><br>The **OPTIONAL** "t" parameter value conveys the time window reset time for the identified policy.<br>|

## Get an International Standing Order

<a id="opIdGetInternationalStandingOrdersInternationalStandingOrderPaymentId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-standing-orders/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-standing-orders/{InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId}`

Enables a PISP to retrieve the status of an International Standing Order payment.

<h3 id="get-an-international-standing-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId|path|string|true|InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

## Get details of an International Standing Order Payment

<a id="opIdGetInternationalStandingOrdersInternationalStandingOrderPaymentIdPaymentDetails"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:8080/international-standing-orders/string/payment-details \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /international-standing-orders/{InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId}/payment-details`

Enables a PISP to retrieve detailed information on the status of an International Standing Order payment.

<h3 id="get-details-of-an-international-standing-order-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId|path|string|true|InternationalStandingOrderPaymentId|
|x-fapi-auth-date|header|string|false|The time when the PSU last logged in with the TPP. <br>All dates in the HTTP headers are represented as RFC 7231 Full Dates. An example is below: <br>Sun, 10 Sep 2017 19:43:31 UTC|
|x-fapi-customer-ip-address|header|string|false|The PSU's IP address if the PSU is currently logged in with the TPP.|
|x-fapi-interaction-id|header|string|false|An RFC4122 UID used as a correlation id.|
|Authorization|header|string|true|An Authorisation Token as per https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6750|
|x-customer-user-agent|header|string|false|Indicates the user-agent that the PSU is using.|
|x-client-id|header|string|false|Only used if an ASPSP requires the client ID in order to return rate limit headers. <br><br>TPPs __must__ refer to ASPSP developer portals for further information on any rate limit policies, if the headers are supported and any additional requirements.<br><br>This header __must not__ be used for client authentication<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_Frequency_1">Frequency_1</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemafrequency_1"></a>
<a id="schema_Frequency_1"></a>
<a id="tocSfrequency_1"></a>
<a id="tocsfrequency_1"></a>

```json
"string"
```

Individual Definitions:
NotKnown - Not Known
EvryDay - Every day
EvryWorkgDay - Every working day
IntrvlDay - An interval specified in number of calendar days (02 to 31)
IntrvlWkDay - An interval specified in weeks (01 to 09), and the day within the week (01 to 07)
WkInMnthDay - A monthly interval, specifying the week of the month (01 to 05) and day within the week (01 to 07)
IntrvlMnthDay - An interval specified in months (between 01 to 06, 12, 24), specifying the day within the month (-05 to -01, 01 to 31)
QtrDay - Quarterly (either ENGLISH, SCOTTISH, or RECEIVED)
ENGLISH = Paid on the 25th March, 24th June, 29th September and 25th December.
SCOTTISH = Paid on the 2nd February, 15th May, 1st August and 11th November.
RECEIVED = Paid on the 20th March, 19th June, 24th September and 20th December.
Individual Patterns:
NotKnown (ScheduleCode)
EvryDay (ScheduleCode)
EvryWorkgDay (ScheduleCode)
IntrvlDay:NoOfDay (ScheduleCode + NoOfDay)
IntrvlWkDay:IntervalInWeeks:DayInWeek (ScheduleCode + IntervalInWeeks + DayInWeek)
WkInMnthDay:WeekInMonth:DayInWeek (ScheduleCode + WeekInMonth + DayInWeek)
IntrvlMnthDay:IntervalInMonths:DayInMonth (ScheduleCode + IntervalInMonths + DayInMonth)
QtrDay: + either (ENGLISH, SCOTTISH or RECEIVED) ScheduleCode + QuarterDay
The regular expression for this element combines five smaller versions for each permitted pattern. To aid legibility - the components are presented individually here:
NotKnown
EvryDay
EvryWorkgDay
IntrvlDay:((0[2-9])|([1-2][0-9])|3[0-1])
IntrvlWkDay:0[1-9]:0[1-7]
WkInMnthDay:0[1-5]:0[1-7]
IntrvlMnthDay:(0[1-6]|12|24):(-0[1-5]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])
QtrDay:(ENGLISH|SCOTTISH|RECEIVED)
Full Regular Expression:
^(NotKnown)$|^(EvryDay)$|^(EvryWorkgDay)$|^(IntrvlDay:((0[2-9])|([1-2][0-9])|3[0-1]))$|^(IntrvlWkDay:0[1-9]:0[1-7])$|^(WkInMnthDay:0[1-5]:0[1-7])$|^(IntrvlMnthDay:(0[1-6]|12|24):(-0[1-5]|0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01]))$|^(QtrDay:(ENGLISH|SCOTTISH|RECEIVED))$

Information that locates and identifies a specific address, as defined by postal services.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|AddressType|[OBAddressType2Code](#schemaobaddresstype2code)|false|none|Identifies the nature of the postal address. For a full set of codes see `OBAddressType2Code` [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets).|
|Department|[Department](#schemadepartment)|false|none|Identification of a division of a large organisation or building.|
|SubDepartment|[SubDepartment](#schemasubdepartment)|false|none|Identification of a sub-division of a large organisation or building.|
|StreetName|[StreetName](#schemastreetname)|false|none|Name of a street or thoroughfare.|
|BuildingNumber|[BuildingNumber](#schemabuildingnumber)|false|none|Number that identifies the position of a building on a street.|
|BuildingName|[BuildingName](#schemabuildingname)|false|none|Name of a referenced building.|
|Floor|[Floor](#schemafloor)|false|none|Number that identifies the level within a building|
|UnitNumber|[UnitNumber](#schemaunitnumber)|false|none|Number that identifies the unit of a specific address .|
|Room|[Room](#schemaroom)|false|none|Information that locates and identifies a room to form part of an address|
|PostBox|[PostBox](#schemapostbox)|false|none|Information that locates and identifies a box in a post office assigned to a person or organization, where letters for them are kept until called for.|
|TownLocationName|[TownName](#schematownname)|false|none|Name of a built-up area, with defined boundaries, and a local government.|
|DistrictName|[DistrictName](#schemadistrictname)|false|none|Number that of the regional area, known as a district, which forms part of an address|
|CareOf|[CareOf](#schemacareof)|false|none|The 'care of' address is used whenever sending mail to a person or organisation who does not actually live or work at the address. They will receive the mail for the individual.|
|PostCode|[PostCode](#schemapostcode)|false|none|Identifier consisting of a group of letters and/or numbers that is added to a postal address to assist the sorting of mail.|
|TownName|[TownName](#schematownname)|false|none|Name of a built-up area, with defined boundaries, and a local government.|
|CountrySubDivision|[CountrySubDivision](#schemacountrysubdivision)|false|none|Identifies a subdivision of a country such as state, region, county.|
|Country|[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)|false|none|Nation with its own government.|
|AddressLine|[string]|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_OBSCASupportData1">OBSCASupportData1</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaobscasupportdata1"></a>
<a id="schema_OBSCASupportData1"></a>
<a id="tocSobscasupportdata1"></a>
<a id="tocsobscasupportdata1"></a>

```json
{
  "RequestedSCAExemptionType": "BillPayment",
  "AppliedAuthenticationApproach": "CA",
  "ReferencePaymentOrderId": "string"
}
```

Supporting Data provided by TPP, when requesting SCA Exemption.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|string|false|none|This field allows a PISP to request specific SCA Exemption for a Payment Initiation. For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalSCAExemptionType1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|AppliedAuthenticationApproach|string|false|none|Specifies a character string with a maximum length of 40 characters.<br>Usage: This field indicates whether the PSU was subject to SCA performed by the TPP<br>For a full list of values refer to `OBInternalAppliedAuthenticationApproach1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|ReferencePaymentOrderId|string|false|none|If the payment is recurring, then this field is populated with the transaction identifier of the previous payment occurrence so that the ASPSP can verify that the PISP, amount and the payee are the same as the previous occurrence. The value here refers to the payment id e.g. DomesticPaymentId  |

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|BillPayment|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|ContactlessTravel|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|EcommerceGoods|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|EcommerceServices|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|Kiosk|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|Parking|
|RequestedSCAExemptionType|PartyToParty|
|AppliedAuthenticationApproach|CA|
|AppliedAuthenticationApproach|SCA|

<h2 id="tocS_OBStatusReason">OBStatusReason</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaobstatusreason"></a>
<a id="schema_OBStatusReason"></a>
<a id="tocSobstatusreason"></a>
<a id="tocsobstatusreason"></a>

```json
{
  "StatusReasonCode": "ERIN",
  "StatusReasonDescription": "string",
  "Path": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|StatusReasonCode|string|false|none|Specifies the status reason in a code form. <br>For a full list of values refer to `OBExternalStatusReason1Code` in *OB_Internal_CodeSet* [here](https://github.com/OpenBankingUK/External_Internal_CodeSets)|
|StatusReasonDescription|string|false|none|Description supporting the StatusReasonCode.|
|Path|string|false|none|Path is optional but relevant when the status reason refers to an object/field and hence conditional to provide JSON path.|

<h2 id="tocS_OBStructuredRegulatoryReporting3">OBStructuredRegulatoryReporting3</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaobstructuredregulatoryreporting3"></a>
<a id="schema_OBStructuredRegulatoryReporting3"></a>
<a id="tocSobstructuredregulatoryreporting3"></a>
<a id="tocsobstructuredregulatoryreporting3"></a>

```json
{
  "Type": "string",
  "Date": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "Country": "string",
  "Amount": {
    "Amount": "string",
    "Currency": "string"
  },
  "Information": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

Set of elements used to provide details on the regulatory reporting information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Type|string|false|none|Specifies the type of the information supplied in the regulatory reporting details|
|Date|[ISODateTime](#schemaisodatetime)|false|none|All dates in the JSON payloads are represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. <br>All date-time fields in responses must include the timezone. An example is below:<br>2017-04-05T10:43:07+00:00|
|Country|[CountryCode](#schemacountrycode)|false|none|Nation with its own government.|
|Amount|[OBActiveOrHistoricCurrencyAndAmount](#schemaobactiveorhistoriccurrencyandamount)|false|none|Amount of money associated with the charge type.|
|Information|[string]|false|none|Additional details that cater for specific domestic regulatory requirements. |

<h2 id="tocS_Time">Time</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematime"></a>
<a id="schema_Time"></a>
<a id="tocStime"></a>
<a id="tocstime"></a>

```json
"00:00:00Z"
```

Time at which assets become available to the account owner in case of a credit entry, or cease to be available to the account owner in case of a debit transaction entry.
Usage: If transaction entry status is pending and value date is present, then the value date refers to an expected/requested value date.
For transaction entries subject to availability/float and for which availability information is provided, the value date must not be used. In this case the availability component identifies the number of availability days. All dates in the JSON payloads are represented in ISO 8601 date-time format. 
All date-time fields in responses must include the timezone. An example is below:
T10:43:07+00:00
